title: Introduce presubmit-minifier and toolchain fingerprinting to reduce CI noise
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a lightweight presubmit minifier that narrows test/lint jobs for small changes; introduces deterministic toolchain fingerprinting to avoid unnecessary dependency installs. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit pipelines are a major contributor to long CI cycles and noisy builds for trivial changes. Multiple teams reported that small README/docs/infra tweaks still trigger full lint/test matrices and expensive toolchain installs. This PR implements two coordinated improvements: (1) a presubmit-minifier that computes a change fingerprint and narrows the set of lint/test shards and the set of tools required for the change, and (2) a toolchain fingerprint file that records the computed toolchain signature per workspace so runners can conditionally reuse cached tool images rather than reinstalling devdeps on every job. The goals are: faster feedback for small diffs, fewer spurious dep installs, and clearer CI cost accounting.

What this PR changes (high level):
- New presubmit-minifier binary (cmd/presubmit-minifier) with a small decision engine that maps changed paths, file globs, and heuristics to a presubmit profile. The profile controls which lint plugins and test groups run.
- Toolchain fingerprinting: a deterministic SHA256-based fingerprint written to .toolchain/fingerprint.json (human-readable) when CI bootstraps. Runners and local devcontainer helpers read this to skip reinstallation if the fingerprint matches cached images.
- CI workflow updates: main/.github/workflows/presubmit.yml updated to call presubmit-minifier and pass profile tags to job matrices; added a lightweight matrix fallback for cases where heuristics are disabled.
- Presubmit daemon unit tests and e2e harnesses under infra/presubmit/tests.
- Docs: docs/dev/presubmit-minifier.md and docs/dev/toolchain-fingerprinting.md.

Commits summary (top-level, chronological):
- feat(presubmit): add presubmit-minifier command and core heuristics
- chore(ci): wire presubmit-minifier into presubmit workflow and matrix expansion
- feat(toolchain): add deterministic fingerprint generator and caching helpers
- test(presubmit): add unit tests and e2e harness for minifier
- docs(ci): add developer docs and rollout plan
- fix(ci): handle edge-case for binary changes affecting fingerprinting

Note: commits were squashed on merge to a single consolidated commit describing the feature.

Files / areas touched (representative):
- cmd/presubmit-minifier/* (new)
- internal/presubmit/heuristics.go
- internal/presubmit/profile_map.yaml
- .toolchain/fingerprint.go
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml
- infra/presubmit/tests/*
- docs/dev/presubmit-minifier.md
- docs/dev/toolchain-fingerprinting.md
- devcontainer/scripts/cache-toolchain.sh
- scripts/ci/cache-check.sh

Behavior and heuristics detail: The minifier inspects the git diff for the PR (base..head) and assigns tags: docs-only, infra-only, service-api, runtime, cross-repo. Each tag maps to a presubmit profile defined in profile_map.yaml. Profiles specify a whitelist of lint plugins and test groups. Heuristics include path-based rules (e.g., docs/** => docs-only), filetype rules (.md, .rst), and a small opt-out annotation "[ci full]" in PR body to force a full run. The fingerprint generator canonicalizes tool versions declared in devcontainer.json and known tool-lock files, sorts entries, and computes a SHA256; the fingerprint is compared against the runner-side cached-image manifest.

Rollout plan and safety net:
- Feature gate enabled in main for all repos but defaults to conservative profiles (i.e., only skip heavyweight jobs for docs-only/infra-only).
- Added a staged rollout: dev teams opt-in by setting presubmit: fast in repo settings; after two weeks of telemetary validation we broaden to default-on for small PRs.
- A fallback matrix job runs in parallel for a sparse sample (5% of PRs) to validate correctness and catch false-negatives in heuristics.
- Opt-out: PR body can include "[ci full]" to force full presubmit.

Review conversation (abridged, inline):
- Claire: "Can heuristics accidentally skip required integration tests when only manifest changes are present?" Author reply: "Good catch — we added a manifest rule to map changes to 'service-api' if CHANGELOG or api/manifest.yaml changes are present, and we keep a conservative default that retains integration tests unless it's docs-only or infra-only."
- Diego: "Toolchain fingerprint files in the repo — will they cause churn?" Author reply: "Fingerprint is written to .toolchain/fingerprint.json but only updated via an explicit `./dev-toolchain regenerate` flow described in docs. CI sets an env guard so it doesn't auto-commit changes. The fingerprint is intended to be human-managed in tandem with devcontainer/tooling upgrades."
- Samir: "How do we validate runner caches aren't stale across cloud images?" Author reply: "Added cache-check.sh that cross-validates stored manifest entries and the artifact registry. We also added telemetry if cache reuses happen more than 3x without observed tests — it will surface as a warning in the presubmit console."
- Claire (after review): "LGTM after small nits (doc clarifications)."
- Diego: "Approved."

CI and validation notes:
- First CI run failed two long-running integration shards due to a flaky infra test; those were retried individually via the rerun action and passed.
- Lint and unit tests passed on first run.
- E2E harness required a minor time adjustment (increased tunable waiter to 30s) to stabilize on slower runner types; that change is in the final commit.

Observability and telemetry:
- Added lightweight presubmit telemetry events: presubmit.profile_assigned and presubmit.fingerprint_mismatch. These are routed to internal metrics and are visible in the presubmit dashboard.
- Telemetry will be sampled initially (10%) to limit noisy dashboards.

Risk assessment:
- False-negatives (skipping required jobs) are the primary risk; mitigations include conservative default profiles, a 5% parallel validation fallback, opt-out override, and telemetry alerts.
- Toolchain fingerprint churn is mitigated by an explicit regenerate flow and docs to guide teams.

Post-merge tasks and follow-ups:
- ENG-1245: sweep repos in the org to add lightweight profile hints for monorepos with many generated files.
- ENG-2208: add an autosuggest feature in the PR UI to propose profile tags when presubmit-minifier produces low confidence.

Merge outcome and method: Squash-and-merge to main with a single consolidated commit titled "presubmit: introduce minifier + toolchain fingerprinting (ENG-1245, ENG-2208)".

Additional notes: This PR was designed to be minimally invasive: when presubmit-minifier is disabled (feature-flag off), the CI behaves exactly as before. We kept the default conservative to avoid regressions. The docs include a rollback procedure and diagnostics for any team that wants to disable local minification in their repo.
